lines.en: Rui, the rules were different when I was a student. We had to wear a uniform, and we weren’t allowed to use our phones.
lines.pt: Rui, as regras eram diferentes quando eu era estudante. Tínhamos que usar uniforme e não podíamos usar celular.

lines.en: Here, the students don’t have to wear a uniform now, and they’re allowed to keep their phones in the bag.
lines.pt: Aqui, os alunos não precisam mais usar uniforme, e podem manter o celular na mochila.

lines.en: That’s a big change. In my time, if a teacher saw a phone, we had to hand it in until the end of term.
lines.pt: Isso é uma grande mudança. No meu tempo, se um professor visse um celular, tínhamos que entregá-lo até o fim do semestre.

lines.en: That’s harsh. We were allowed to bring ours, but we couldn’t answer calls in class.
lines.pt: Isso é duro. Podíamos levar o nosso, mas não podíamos atender ligações na aula.

lines.en: Did you have to stay after school if you broke a rule? I remember cleaning the gym for a whole week.
lines.pt: Você tinha que ficar depois da aula se quebrasse uma regra? Lembro de limpar o ginásio por uma semana inteira.

lines.en: Yes, detention was normal. But we didn’t have to do homework on Fridays, so the weekend felt long and free.
lines.pt: Sim, detenção era normal. Mas não tínhamos que fazer lição de casa às sextas, então o fim de semana parecia longo e livre.

lines.en: Lucky you. Our headmaster was so strict that we had to stand up whenever an adult came in.
lines.pt: Sorte sua. Nosso diretor era tão rígido que tínhamos que ficar de pé sempre que um adulto entrava na sala.

lines.en: Really? Were you allowed to eat in the corridors, or did you have to go outside, even in winter?
lines.pt: Sério? Vocês podiam comer nos corredores, ou tinham que ir lá fora, mesmo no inverno?

lines.en: We had to go outside, and nobody was allowed to stay in the classrooms during the break, which was exhausting.
lines.pt: Tínhamos que ir lá fora, e ninguém podia ficar nas salas durante o intervalo, o que era cansativo.

lines.en: Maybe that’s why you became so independent. I admit I miss some old traditions, though.
lines.pt: Talvez por isso você aprendeu a ser tão independente. Admito que sinto falta de algumas tradições antigas.

lines.en: So do I. Let’s walk around the building and see whether the old bell still rings at the same time.
lines.pt: Eu também. Vamos andar pelo prédio e ver se o velho sino ainda toca no mesmo horário.

pages.title: The old school · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny afternoon in Denver. Dirk stops in front of an old school. Rui joins him near the gate. Students leave with bags. Nothing looks the same. They smile at the old bell.

“Rui, the rules were different when I was a student. We had to wear a uniform, and we weren’t allowed to use our phones.” says Dirk. “Here, the students don’t have to wear a uniform now, and they’re allowed to keep their phones in the bag.” says Rui. “That’s a big change. In my time, if a teacher saw a phone, we had to hand it in until the end of term.” says Dirk.
